title: A Suspected Primary May Still Be Writing
description: Monitoring cannot reach the primary, but some clients still can. The team wants to promote a standby. What must the failover protocol establish?

options.text: A failed health check proves the old primary has stopped.
options.explanation: A timeout can reflect a partition, not a dead process. The old primary may remain reachable elsewhere.

options.text: Any replica has every acknowledged write because replication is enabled.
options.explanation: An asynchronous or insufficiently durable replica can lack acknowledged changes.

options.text: Fence the old authority, choose an appropriate replica and publish the new primary to clients.
options.explanation: Coordination and fencing prevent two authoritative writers. Replica progress determines possible data loss, and clients and pools need a discovery/reconnect path.

options.text: Increase read-replica count instead of coordinating promotion.
options.explanation: More copies do not decide ownership or revoke the old primary's write authority.
